about.title: Boring systems, in the best sense of the word
paragraphs: I work at both ends of a system's life. On one side, mission-critical legacy in the energy sector — Java 8, JSF, EJB — where an export that times out means a late regulatory report. On the other, reactive banking microservices in Java 21 and Kotlin, with WebFlux, Redis and circuit breakers absorbing peak load. Both ends teach the same lesson from opposite directions: what counts is shipping without taking down the business that is already running.

I like systems that are predictable, observable and easy for the next person to touch. In practice that means hexagonal architecture with a framework-free domain, decisions recorded in ADRs rather than in the author's memory, and tests that run against the real service through Testcontainers. I am currently doing a postgraduate diploma in Software Architecture at FIAP and writing plenty of Kotlin, Go and — lately — AI application infrastructure with MCP and RAG.
